name: three-studio
description: 3D game editor built on Three.js and Electron

scripts.dev: npm run build:web && npm run dev --workspace @three-studio/desktop
scripts.build: npm run build:web && npm run build --workspace @three-studio/desktop
scripts.//build:packages: Publish order, not preference: the build configs clear the root `paths`, so runtime and editor resolve `@three-studio/core` the way a consumer does — through node_modules, to a dist that has to exist already.
scripts.build:packages: npm run build --workspace @three-studio/core && npm run build --workspace @three-studio/runtime && npm run build --workspace @three-studio/editor
scripts.dist: npm run build:web && npm run dist --workspace @three-studio/desktop
scripts.//dist: There is deliberately no dist:all. esbuild is a runtime dependency — the packaged app compiles user scripts with it — and npm installs only the host platform's binary, so packaging --win from a Mac yields an installer that launches and then cannot compile a single script. Nothing in the build fails. Cross-platform packaging goes through .github/workflows/release.yml, one native runner per target.
scripts.dist:mac: npm run build:web && npm run dist:mac --workspace @three-studio/desktop
scripts.dist:win: npm run build:web && npm run dist:win --workspace @three-studio/desktop
scripts.dist:linux: npm run build:web && npm run dist:linux --workspace @three-studio/desktop
scripts.//postinstall: three's FBXLoader reads LayerElementNormal[0].Normals without checking it is there, while guarding Colors and UV in the very same function. An FBX that declares a normal layer and leaves it empty — which is what an Unreal UCX_ collision hull is — throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading a)', and the throw loses the whole file rather than the one empty layer: the mesh next to it never arrives either. Still unfixed on three's dev branch at 0.185.1, so patches/three+0.185.1.patch adds the guard and this reapplies it after every install.

//optionalDependencies: npm does not record lightningcss's own optionalDependencies in the lockfile (npm/cli#4828), so its native binary is dropped on the next install and Tailwind fails with 'Cannot find module ../lightningcss.<platform>.node'. Declaring them here puts them in the lockfile; each carries os/cpu guards, so only the matching one is ever installed.
